headline: Rolling compass, first answer: switching afternoon setups off after a midday flip does not help on 2 years (coin-flip counts); the coil setups trade before noon, so a morning on/off rule is tested next.
bullets: Flip study on 357,664 two-year afternoon trades: after a flip, setups did worse in only 27-30 of ~65 family-sides; standby beat a random block in only ~half - for all 3 flip definitions.
Live (25 sessions): only one midday flip (11-02, -85R aligned trades after it); on 2 years flips happen on 16-26% of days.
'Trading against the morning reading' looked costly, but it is market direction plus look-ahead in the label - not a lead.
Closed too: skipping flow-sell shorts at a fresh low (0 of 2 on 2 years).
Next: one pre-registered morning on/off rule for the coil setups (bar t 3.57), then a forward shadow.
next: Scout freezes the coil morning rule; Builder scores it and builds an overfitting check (PBO); Observer maps where morning conditions matter.
